$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}CX & =\sqrt{{(-6-2)}^{2}+{(6-0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our circle is generated by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & =(10)^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+y^{2} & =100\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

The length of the radius is 

$$
\begin{aligned}CX & =\sqrt{{(-8-(- \frac{9}{2}))}^{2}+{(-3-(- \frac{7}{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(- \frac{7}{2})^{2}+{\frac{1}{2}}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our circle is generated by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-(- \frac{9}{2}))^{2}+(y-(- \frac{7}{2}))^{2} & =(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2})^{2} \\ (x+\frac{9}{2})^{2}+(y+\frac{7}{2})^{2} & =\frac{25}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
